Buffer 3D points or lines into polygons

Source: R/buffer_3d.R
buffer_3d.Rd

Draws a polygon around each point or line of a SpatVector3D, with a depth range and an optional time interval, as sf::st_buffer() does in 2D. A detection at 35 m with radius_km = 10 and depth_window = 25 becomes a circle of 10 km radius from 10 to 60 m deep.

Usage

buffer_3d(x, radius_km, depth_window, time_window = NULL)

Arguments

x

A SpatVector3D of points or lines, from as_vector3d().

radius_km

Horizontal radius in kilometres: one positive number, below 10000.

depth_window

Depth in metres added above and below each feature's depths: one number, 0 or more. The top stops at the surface (0 m). With 0, the polygon spans just the feature's own depth range.

time_window

Optional time added before and after each feature's times: a number of days, or a difftime (e.g. as.difftime(6, units = "hours")). Every vertex needs a time. If x has dates without hours, the window must be whole days, and the interval covers whole UTC days as in as_vector3d(). With NULL (default), each polygon keeps its feature's own times: a point's time, a line's first to last time, or no time. A line with times at some vertices but not others is an error either way.

Value

A SpatVector3D of polygons, one per feature of x, with the same IDs. For points, the other columns of x are kept. For lines, columns with one value along each line (such as a tag name) are kept, and columns that change from vertex to vertex (such as speed) are dropped.

Details

The outline is a circle (for a line, the area within radius_km of it) measured on the WGS84 ellipsoid, made with terra::buffer(). Outlines that cross the 180th meridian (the antimeridian) are split there into two parts.

Each polygon has one depth range and one time interval, so a line's polygon covers the line's whole depth and time range. Depth runs from depth_window above the shallowest vertex to depth_window below the deepest, and time from time_window before the first time to time_window after the last. For a dive from the surface to 300 m, the polygon spans 0 m to 300 m plus depth_window along the whole track. To follow the dive more closely, split the line into shorter lines or points and buffer those.

See also

as_vector3d(), geomtype()

Examples

obs <- data.frame(lon = c(150, 151), lat = c(-20, -21), depth = c(35, 120),
                  date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-02")))
detections <- as_vector3d(obs, time = "date")

# 10 km circles, 25 m above and below each detection, a day either side.
buffers <- buffer_3d(detections, radius_km = 10, depth_window = 25,
                     time_window = 1)
as.data.frame(buffers)[c("feature_id", "depth_min", "depth_max",
                         "time_start", "time_end")]
#>   feature_id depth_min depth_max time_start   time_end
#> 1          1        10        60 2019-12-31 2020-01-02
#> 2          2        95       145 2020-01-01 2020-01-03

# A corridor 5 km either side of a dive track.
dive <- data.frame(tag = "A", lon = c(150, 150.1, 150.2), lat = -20,
                   depth = c(0, 120, 15))
track <- as_vector3d(dive, type = "lines", id = "tag")
buffer_3d(track, radius_km = 5, depth_window = 10)
#> class      : SpatVector3D
#> geometry   : polygons 
#> features   : 1 
#> depth (m)  : 0 to 130 
#> time       : none
